info.name: Game Tracker Service
info.description:
Complete API collection for the Game Tracker Service.

## Setup
1. Import this collection into Postman.
2. Set the `baseUrl` variable to your running instance (default: `http://localhost:3000`).
3. Set the `adminApiKey` variable to the value of `ADMIN_API_KEY` in your `.env` file.

## Workflow
A typical testing flow:
1. **Health** — verify the service is up and the DB is reachable.
2. **Create a game** — use the *Admin > Create Game* request; the response `id` is automatically saved to the `gameId` variable.
3. **Read the game** — use *Public > Get Game by ID* to see the composed view.
4. **Add a manual source** — the returned `_id` is saved to `sourceId`.
5. **Create an override** — the returned `_id` is saved to `overrideId`.
6. **List, patch, delete** — explore the rest of the admin endpoints.
7. **Trigger ingestion** — fire *Admin > Trigger Ingestion Run* to run the pipeline on demand.

1. Canonical game data

item.name: Admin — Manual Sources
item.description:
Admin endpoints for managing manual sources attached to games. All requests require the `X-Admin-Key` header.

Manual sources are additional URLs or claims you attach to a game record. They are scoped to different parts of the composed view:
- `general` — attached to the top-level sources array
- `release` — scoped to release date evidence
- `seasonWindow` — scoped to season start/end window evidence
- `media` — scoped to media content

request.description:
Attach a manual source to a game. The `scope` controls where it appears in the composed view.

The response `_id` is automatically saved to the `sourceId` collection variable.

item.name: Admin — Overrides
item.description:
Admin endpoints for managing field-level overrides. All requests require the `X-Admin-Key` header.

An override is a `Partial<Game>` patch applied at read time via a deep merge (arrays are replaced, not merged). Only **one** override can be `enabled: true` per game — enabling a new one automatically disables the previous one.

This is the preferred way to make reversible corrections to ingested data.

request.description:
Create an override and enable it immediately. Any previously enabled override for this game is automatically disabled.

The response `_id` is automatically saved to the `overrideId` collection variable.

response.name: 201 Created

request.description: Create an override as a draft (disabled). Enable it later with the PATCH endpoint.
Enable a previously disabled override. Any previously enabled override for the same game is automatically disabled.
Disable an active override. The game will revert to its canonical ingested data.
Update the patch content of an existing override without changing its enabled state.

item.name: Admin — Ingestion
item.description:
Admin endpoints for the data ingestion pipeline. Requires the `X-Admin-Key` header.

The ingestion pipeline runs automatically at 03:00 UTC on the 1st and 15th of every month. Use these endpoints to trigger it on demand or check run history.

request.description:
Trigger the full ingestion pipeline immediately. The run executes in the background; this endpoint returns `202 Accepted` as soon as the run starts.

Check the `ingestion_runs` collection in MongoDB for run status and per-game results.

**What the pipeline does:**
1. Loads all games from the database
2. Calls each applicable provider (Steam, IGDB, Epic, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo)
3. Discovers new source URLs via the crawler
4. Merges and upserts results back into the `games` collection
5. Records run metadata in `ingestion_runs`
